suggestions: pre-filter a large table as a CTE before the join
split an OR predicate into UNION ALL branches
reorder joins to reduce intermediate rows
use CTE for date filtering and mapping
replace rollup with explicit grouping and filtering
use dense rank in subquery to filter early
reached_sql:
WITH months AS (
    SELECT d_date_sk,
           d_year,
           d_qoy,
           d_moy
    FROM date_dim
    WHERE d_month_seq BETWEEN 1217 AND 1217+11
),
fact AS (
    SELECT ss.ss_item_sk,
           ss.ss_store_sk,
           ss.ss_sold_date_sk,
           SUM(COALESCE(ss.ss_sales_price * ss.ss_quantity, 0)) AS sumsales
    FROM store_sales ss
    WHERE ss.ss_sold_date_sk IN (SELECT months.d_date_sk FROM months)
    GROUP BY ss.ss_item_sk, ss.ss_store_sk, ss.ss_sold_date_sk
),
dw1 AS (
    SELECT i.i_category,
           i.i_class,
           i.i_brand,
           i.i_product_name,
           m.d_year,
           m.d_qoy,
           m.d_moy,
           st.s_store_id,
           SUM(f.sumsales) AS sumsales
    FROM fact f
    JOIN item i ON f.ss_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    JOIN store st ON f.ss_store_sk = st.s_store_sk
    JOIN months m ON f.ss_sold_date_sk = m.d_date_sk
    GROUP BY ROLLUP(i.i_category, i.i_class, i.i_brand, i.i_product_name,
                    m.d_year, m.d_qoy, m.d_moy, st.s_store_id)
),
dw1_filtered AS (
    SELECT ranked_dw1.i_category,
           ranked_dw1.i_class,
           ranked_dw1.i_brand,
           ranked_dw1.i_product_name,
           ranked_dw1.d_year,
           ranked_dw1.d_qoy,
           ranked_dw1.d_moy,
           ranked_dw1.s_store_id,
           ranked_dw1.sumsales
    FROM (
        SELECT dw1.*,
               DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY i_category ORDER BY sumsales DESC) AS drk
        FROM dw1
    ) ranked_dw1
    WHERE ranked_dw1.drk <= 100
),
dw2 AS (
    SELECT i_category,
           i_class,
           i_brand,
           i_product_name,
           d_year,
           d_qoy,
           d_moy,
           s_store_id,
           sumsales,
           RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY i_category ORDER BY sumsales DESC) AS rk
    FROM dw1_filtered
)
SELECT i_category,
       i_class,
       i_brand,
       i_product_name,
       d_year,
       d_qoy,
       d_moy,
       s_store_id,
       sumsales,
       rk
FROM dw2
WHERE rk <= 100
ORDER BY i_category,
         i_class,
         i_brand,
         i_product_name,
         d_year,
         d_qoy,
         d_moy,
         s_store_id,
         sumsales,
         rk
LIMIT 100

1. COVERING INDEX-ONLY MONTH SCAN — TARGET: `store_sales` (`ss_sold_date_sk`, `ss_item_sk`, `ss_store_sk`, `ss_sales_price`, `ss_quantity`) — TRANSFORMATION: Create a covering index on `store_sales(ss_sold_date_sk) INCLUDE (ss_item_sk, ss_store_sk, ss_sales_price, ss_quantity)` and drive the `d_month_seq = 1217..1228` date window through that index, so the large fact-table access becomes an index-only range scan instead of a full heap scan.

2. FACT-GRAIN PRE-AGGREGATION BEFORE DIMENSION JOINS — TARGET: the inner `store_sales` join to `item`, `store`, and `date_dim` feeding `GROUP BY ROLLUP` — TRANSFORMATION: On the already date-pruned `store_sales` rows, first aggregate by `(ss_item_sk, ss_store_sk, ss_sold_date_sk)` to compute `SUM(ss_sales_price*ss_quantity)`, then join this compacted result to `item`, `store`, and `date_dim`; this reduces the ROLLUP input from individual sales line-items to one row per item/store/date before the expensive multi-level grouping.

3. TOP-100 SUMSALES THRESHOLD PRE-FILTER — TARGET: the `dw1` row set feeding `rank() OVER (PARTITION BY i_category ORDER BY sumsales DESC)` — TRANSFORMATION: Before applying the window, restrict `dw1` to rows whose `sumsales` is among the 100 largest distinct `sumsales` values for that `i_category` (keeping all rows when fewer than 100 distinct values exist); rows below that threshold cannot have `rk <= 100`, so the window sort and rank computation only process true candidate rows.

4. COVERING DATE-DIMENSION INDEX — TARGET: `date_dim.d_month_seq`, `d_date_sk`, `d_year`, `d_qoy`, `d_moy` — TRANSFORMATION: Add a covering index on `date_dim(d_month_seq, d_date_sk)` including `d_year`, `d_qoy`, and `d_moy`, so resolving the 12-month predicate to exact date keys and later projecting the date attributes is a single index-only lookup, avoiding repeated small-dimension heap accesses at join time.
